thought.text: Now rerun `install.sh` (it's idempotent for a not-yet-locked instance):

reasoning_content:
Next, let's re-run install.sh. It's idempotent: it will re-run apt-get (already installed, so fast), re-render the configuration, etc. Since LOCK_FILE does not exist, it will proceed. Also, it will retry `systemctl enable --now mariadb`, but the bootstrap user creation happens before the final Apache restart.

One concern: on re-run, `ensure_link_target_available` for /etc/apache2/sites-available/qisutu.conf — on the first run, the symbolic link was created (the script failed after the apt phase, at `systemctl enable --now "$DB_SERVICE"` (around line 720) — actually, did it get that far? The apt phase completed, and then verify_perl_modules, verify_apache_modules, ensure_qisutu_runtime_user, directories, permissions, security keys, tmpfiles, configure_selinux (skipped on debian), configure_firewall (no firewalld), systemd unit rendering (daemon + install-complete path/service), daemon-reload, enable --now mariadb → the shim failed → set -e exited. So the state: instance.conf written, systemd units written (qisutu-daemon.service, qisutu-install-complete.service/.path), Apache configuration symlink created and a2ensite done, Apache service not started, MariaDB not started, no bootstrap user.

Re-run: no problems, idempotent.

Alright, let's re-run now.
